A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the convergence of a (block coordinate) descent method is shown for a large class of nondifferentiable functions, which are not assumed to be convex.

the convergence results of the block coordinate descent method are stronger than the corresponding convergence results of the gradient projection method for minimizing a convex function.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the class of problems considered, the convergence rate of the coordinate descent algorithm is not slower than the convergence rate of a proximal minimization method, and, in some cases, it can be faster.
the block coordinate descent method is a powerful tool for the study of convergence properties of a variety of algorithms for nondifferentiable optimization problems.
